{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01B864DM1HUeGxbf55WeBaHY","type":"tool_result","content":"=== persistence/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n=== persistence/testing.py\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit; the criterion owns idempotent recovery and business cleanup.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database\n=== persistence/db.py\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies; for ``get``, ``list``, and ``delete`` they\n    are the predicate, and for ``create`` and ``update`` they are the values written. ``row`` is\n    the dataclass a read or a create returns, and ``columns`` are the columns it selects.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SJkucEeKn8CD66ksMY5iGL","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"SQLite engine for ``db.py``.\n\nShipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here.\n\nSQLite is the development and test engine. It parses the same declaration PostgreSQL does and\nignores what it does not enforce — ``VARCHAR(n)`` length in particular — so one rendered schema\nserves both engines and nothing is stripped for one of them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\ntry:\n    from .db import Driver\nexcept ImportError:  # flat layout\n    from db import Driver\n\n__all__ = [\"SqliteDriver\"]\n\n\nclass SqliteDriver(Driver):\n    \"\"\"One connection per thread, opened on first use in that thread.\n\n    A ``sqlite3.Connection`` belongs to the thread that created it and raises ``ProgrammingError``\n    when used from another, so a single connection opened during construction is valid in no web\n    request at all. This is not concurrency: queries stay sequential within a workflow, and the\n    rule only stops one connection being shared across unrelated ones.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:\n        self._path = _path_from(dsn)\n        self._local = threading.local()\n\n    def connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is None:\n            if self._path != \":memory:\":\n                Path(self._path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            # Autocommit by default; an explicit BEGIN suspends it until ROLLBACK.\n            connection = sqlite3.connect(self._path, isolation_level=None)\n            connection.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL\")\n            connection.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON\")\n            self._local.connection = connection\n        return connection\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is not None:\n            connection.close()\n            self._local.connection = None\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:\n        return cursor.lastrowid\n\n\ndef _path_from(dsn: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Read a filesystem path out of a DSN, accepting a bare path as well as a URL.\"\"\"\n    if \"://\" not in dsn:\n        return dsn or \":memory:\"\n    _, _, remainder = dsn.partition(\"://\")\n    return remainder or \":memory:\"\n---\n..........................                                               [100%]\n26 passed in 0.27s\n---\n/home/barlo/.local/bin/uv\napp.db\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"books\" (\"id\" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, \"title\" TEXT NOT NULL, \"author\" TEXT NOT NULL);","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"15d1c434-769f-4015-8509-723b20028474","uuid":"2b44149c-d581-4727-ac83-ac25ca861540","timestamp":"2026-10-23T14:57:32.012Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"SQLite engine for ``db.py``.\n\nShipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. It parses the same declaration PostgreSQL does and\nignores what it does not enforce — ``VARCHAR(n)`` length in particular — so one rendered schema\nserves both engines and nothing is stripped for one of them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\ntry:\n    from .db import Driver\nexcept ImportError:  # flat layout\n    from db import Driver\n\n__all__ = [\"SqliteDriver\"]\n\n\nclass SqliteDriver(Driver):\n    \"\"\"One connection per thread, opened on first use in that thread.\n\n    A ``sqlite3.Connection`` belongs to the thread that created it and raises ``ProgrammingError``\n    when used from another, so a single connection opened during construction is valid in no web\n    request at all. This is not concurrency: queries stay sequential within a workflow, and the\n    rule only stops one connection being shared across unrelated ones.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:\n        self._path = _path_from(dsn)\n        self._local = threading.local()\n\n    def connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is None:\n            if self._path != \":memory:\":\n                Path(self._path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            # Autocommit by default; an explicit BEGIN suspends it until ROLLBACK.\n            connection = sqlite3.connect(self._path, isolation_level=None)\n            connection.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL\")\n            connection.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON\")\n            self._local.connection = connection\n        return connection\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is not None:\n            connection.close()\n            self._local.connection = None\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:\n        return cursor.lastrowid\n\n\ndef _path_from(dsn: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Read a filesystem path out of a DSN, accepting a bare path as well as a URL.\"\"\"\n    if \"://\" not in dsn:\n        return dsn or \":memory:\"\n    _, _, remainder = dsn.partition(\"://\")\n    return remainder or \":memory:\"\n---\n..........................
